messages:
maria: Quick question — product team wants to send a batch of model outputs to a third-party evaluation vendor (metrics + example completions). Outputs include short user prompts; could contain emails/names. Do we treat these as Confidential by default or can we send after simple redaction? @irfan @audrey

devin: If there are any user identifiers it's Confidential. Need vendor NDA + DPA and an access approval. Also confirm there's no PHI. See data-class link: https://redwood.internal/policy/data-classification :eyes:

irfan: Also consider context length — full convo context is higher risk than single-line prompts/completions. If you redact, do it deterministically and keep a scrub log. Example quick regex to redact emails:

```
s/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/[REDACTED_EMAIL]/g
```

maria: This is just final completions + prompt, usually 1–2 lines. Concern is over-redaction hurting eval quality. Is a whitelisting approach (allow list domains or token masking) okay?

audrey: We can approve if you meet these items: (1) vendor NDA + DPA in place, (2) minimal sample size, (3) PII redacted (emails, phone numbers, IDs), (4) file stored on internal approved bucket and an access request filed in #security-approvals with @audrey as approver. If you upload a scrubbed sample I can fast-track review. :thumbsup:

access-approvals-bot: Access request created: AR-2026-3345 by maria. Status: Pending security review.

maria: Thanks — I created a scrubbed sample and ticket AR-2026-3345 and uploaded to s3://redwood-eval/maria/sample_2026-03-17.csv. I'll open a PR with the redaction script and sample diff. @audrey — pinging you there.

audrey: Got it, I'll take a look and aim to approve by EOD. One more note: if outputs accidentally contain internal config or secret-like tokens treat those as Internal/Restricted and do NOT share. I'll respond in the ticket with any requested changes.
